description: An introduction to the six articles of Islamic faith, the meaning of Tawheed and its categories, and the effect of correct belief on a Muslim's life.

mcq.questionText: How many articles of faith (Arkan al-Iman) are there in Islam?
mcq.explanation: The articles of faith are six: belief in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Decree (Qadar).

mcq.questionText: The Arabic word 'Aqida' is best translated as which of the following?
mcq.explanation: Aqida refers to the firm beliefs or creed that a Muslim holds in the heart with conviction.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is one of the six articles of faith?
mcq.explanation: Belief in the Divine Decree (Qadar) is the sixth article of faith; the others listed are pillars of Islam, not articles of faith.

mcq.questionText: Tawheed means belief in which of the following?
mcq.explanation: Tawheed is the belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, the foundation of Islamic faith.

mcq.questionText: Which holy book was revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses)?
mcq.explanation: The Tawrat (Torah) was the revealed scripture given to Prophet Musa, and belief in the Books is the third article of faith.

mcq.questionText: The angel responsible for delivering revelation to the Prophets is:
mcq.explanation: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) was entrusted with bringing Allah's revelation to His Messengers, including the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad.

mcq.questionText: Belief that Allah alone is the Creator and Sustainer of everything is which category of Tawheed?
mcq.explanation: Tawheed al-Rububiyyah is the oneness of Allah in His lordship, meaning He alone creates, sustains, and governs all things.

mcq.questionText: Which holy book was revealed to Prophet Dawud (David)?
mcq.explanation: The Zabur (Psalms) was the scripture revealed to Prophet Dawud.
Kufr (disbelief) is the opposite of Iman; it is the rejection or denial of the articles of faith.

mcq.questionText: Belief in the Last Day includes belief in:

options.text: Resurrection and the Day of Judgement

mcq.explanation: Belief in the Last Day includes belief in resurrection, the Day of Judgement, and the reward of Paradise or punishment of Hell.

mcq.questionText: Directing all acts of worship to Allah alone is known as:
mcq.explanation: Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah is the oneness of Allah in worship, meaning that all worship must be directed to Him alone.

mcq.questionText: Associating partners with Allah is called:
mcq.explanation: Shirk is the act of associating partners with Allah, which is the gravest sin and the opposite of Tawheed.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following statements about the angels is correct?

options.text: They were created from light and always obey Allah
They eat, drink and sleep like humans

mcq.explanation: Angels were created from light (nur), do not disobey Allah, and carry out the duties assigned to them.

mcq.questionText: Believing that Allah has the most beautiful names and perfect attributes is the category of Tawheed known as:
mcq.explanation: Tawheed al-Asma wa al-Sifat is affirming the beautiful names and perfect attributes of Allah as He has described Himself, without distortion.

mcq.questionText: A Muslim who firmly believes in Qadar will most likely respond to hardship by:

options.text: Being patient and trusting in Allah's wisdom

mcq.explanation: Belief in Divine Decree gives a Muslim patience and contentment, knowing that everything happens by the will and wisdom of Allah.

fib.questionText: The Arabic term for the articles of faith is Arkan al-_____.
fib.explanation: Arkan al-Iman means the pillars or articles of faith, of which there are six.

fib.questionText: Belief in the oneness of Allah is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Tawheed is the central concept of Islamic belief, affirming that Allah is one and unique.

fib.questionText: The holy book revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus) is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The Injil (Gospel) was the revealed scripture given to Prophet Isa.

fib.questionText: Angels were created by Allah from _____.
fib.explanation: According to Islamic teaching, angels were created from light (nur).

fib.questionText: The sixth article of faith is belief in the Divine Decree, known in Arabic as _____.
fib.explanation: Qadar refers to Allah's predestination and the belief that everything happens by His knowledge and will.

fib.questionText: Associating partners with Allah is the gravest sin and is called _____.
fib.explanation: Shirk is the opposite of Tawheed and is considered the most serious sin in Islam.

fib.questionText: The final messenger sent by Allah to all mankind was Prophet _____.
fib.explanation: Prophet Muhammad is the last of the messengers, and belief in the messengers is the fourth article of faith.

fib.questionText: The category of Tawheed concerning Allah's lordship over creation is Tawheed al-_____.
fib.explanation: Tawheed al-Rububiyyah affirms that Allah alone is the Creator, Sustainer, and Master of all things.

fib.questionText: Belief in resurrection and the Day of Judgement is part of belief in the _____ Day.
fib.explanation: Belief in the Last Day is the fifth article of faith and includes resurrection and accountability.

fib.questionText: The angel who brought revelation from Allah to the Prophets is named _____.
fib.explanation: Jibril (Gabriel) is the angel entrusted with delivering Allah's revelation to His messengers.

tf.questionText: There are six articles of faith in Islam.
tf.explanation: The six articles are belief in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Qadar.

tf.questionText: Tawheed means believing in the existence of many gods.
tf.explanation: Tawheed means believing in the oneness of Allah, not many gods; believing in many gods is shirk.

tf.questionText: Angels have free will and can choose to disobey Allah.
tf.explanation: Angels always obey Allah and carry out His commands; they do not disobey Him.

tf.questionText: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad.
tf.explanation: The Qur'an is the final revealed book, given to Prophet Muhammad as guidance for all mankind.

tf.questionText: Belief in the Last Day is one of the pillars of Islam, not an article of faith.
tf.explanation: Belief in the Last Day is one of the six articles of faith, not one of the five pillars of Islam.

tf.questionText: The Tawrat was revealed to Prophet Musa.
tf.explanation: The Tawrat (Torah) was the scripture given to Prophet Musa.

tf.questionText: Qadar means belief in Allah's predestination and divine decree.
tf.explanation: Belief in Qadar means accepting that everything happens by Allah's knowledge, will, and wisdom.

tf.questionText: Correct belief (Aqida) has no effect on how a Muslim behaves in daily life.
tf.explanation: Correct belief shapes a Muslim's character, giving patience, sincerity, honesty, and good conduct.

tf.questionText: Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah means directing all worship to Allah alone.
tf.explanation: Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah is the oneness of Allah in worship, so that no act of worship is given to anyone besides Him.

tf.questionText: Iman (faith) consists only of words on the tongue without belief in the heart.
tf.explanation: True Iman is belief held firmly in the heart, affirmed by the tongue, and acted upon by the limbs.

summary.correctAnswer: Belief in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and Divine Decree (Qadar)
summary.explanation: These six beliefs form the foundation of Iman in Islam.

summary.correctAnswer: Belief in the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah
summary.explanation: Tawheed is the core principle of the Islamic creed.

summary.correctAnswer: Tawheed al-Rububiyyah, Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah, and Tawheed al-Asma wa al-Sifat
summary.explanation: These are oneness in lordship, oneness in worship, and oneness in names and attributes.
Shirk is the gravest sin because it contradicts the oneness of Allah.

summary.explanation: Belief in the revealed Books is the third article of faith.

summary.questionText: What angels are and what they do
summary.correctAnswer: Beings created from light who always obey Allah and carry out His commands
summary.explanation: Belief in angels is the second article of faith.

summary.questionText: Meaning of belief in the Last Day
summary.correctAnswer: Belief in resurrection, the Day of Judgement, and reward in Paradise or punishment in Hell
summary.explanation: This belief encourages accountability and good deeds.

summary.correctAnswer: Belief that everything happens by Allah's knowledge, will, and decree
summary.explanation: Belief in Qadar brings patience, contentment, and trust in Allah.

summary.questionText: Effect of correct belief on a Muslim's life
summary.correctAnswer: It produces patience, sincerity, honesty, good character, and trust in Allah
summary.explanation: Sound Aqida guides a Muslim's actions and gives peace of mind.

summary.correctAnswer: Belief in the heart, affirmation by the tongue, and action by the limbs
summary.explanation: Faith is not merely words but must be confirmed by sincere belief and good deeds.

hoq.questionText: A student says: 'I believe Allah created and controls the universe, but I also pray to a saint to grant my wishes.' Which category of Tawheed has this student failed to fulfil?
hoq.explanation: He affirms Allah as Creator (Rububiyyah) but directs worship to a saint, violating Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah, which requires all worship for Allah alone.

hoq.questionText: Why is belief in the Last Day considered essential for encouraging good moral behaviour in society?

options.text: Because it removes all responsibility from people
Because it teaches that everyone will be held accountable and rewarded or punished for their deeds
Because it allows people to do as they please without consequence
Because it denies the existence of reward and punishment

hoq.explanation: Belief in accountability on the Day of Judgement motivates people to do good and avoid wrong, strengthening morality in society.

hoq.questionText: A believer loses his wealth in a flood yet remains patient and says 'This is from Allah, and there is wisdom in it.' Which article of faith is he most clearly demonstrating?
hoq.explanation: Accepting hardship with patience and trust that it occurs by Allah's decree and wisdom reflects belief in Qadar.
